correctness_checks.g1_corpus_gap: 15 syntcomp25-panel sentinels resolve their TLSF source via tests/suites/benchmarks/syntcomp25/sources.tsv to hash-named paths under a 'syntcomp/<sha256>.ltl' tree. That tree has zero entries in the committed, reconstructable tests/suites/benchmarks/tlsf-manifest.tsv (grep -c '^syntcomp/' = 0) and was not found anywhere on this machine, though the demand-sparse sprint (2 days prior) reported G1 GATE PASS 40/40 -- that corpus has since been lost (not part of any write-protected or hash-pinned evidence directory, so not something this session should reconstruct from a filename). This is a pre-existing environment/tooling gap, not a build or code defect: G0 is clean on both binaries, and every G1 sentinel that could run shows zero verdict changes and zero coverage losses on both B and S. Recorded here rather than silently working around it; does not block the broad campaign per §3.2 (performance/tooling gaps do not veto research, only semantic or memory-safety failures do, and this is neither).

host.affinity_quota_policy: no CPU quota, MemoryMax=8G MemorySwapMax=0 per whole invocation via benchlib.run_systemd_scope (built into run-syntcomp26-coverage.py, no external wrapping needed)
host.sequencing: strictly sequential, one solver invocation at a time, quiet host, no other build/profiling work run concurrently with primary measurement legs

harness.shard_and_order_driver: benchmarking/run-witness-sprint.py (new, thin: shard generation + per-shard/per-epoch B/S order rotation + subprocess dispatch; no independent PAR-2 or scoring logic)
harness.caps_invoked_separately: caps 120 and 17 are always passed as separate --caps N invocations (never --caps 17,120) to avoid the staged-cap runner's earliest-decisive-cap summarization mixing regimes, per §4.1/[S9]
harness.epoch_order: epoch 1 canonical order B,S; each shard alternates starting candidate (even shard index: epoch-base order, odd: reversed); epoch 2 uses the reversed epoch-base order with the same per-shard alternation rule
